**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 102, verses 1–8**

**Explanation of the words:**

**ألهاكم** (alhākum): That is, it occupied you away from obedience to God, the Exalted.

**التكاثر** (al-takāthur): That is, boasting about the abundance of wealth.

**حتى زرتم المقابر** (ḥattā zurtumu al-maqābir): That is, you were preoccupied with gathering wealth and boasting of its abundance until you died and were carried to the graveyards.

**كلا** (kallā): That is, this is not how you should behave, so refrain from this piling up.

**سوف تعلمون** (sawfa ta'lamūn): That is, when you enter your graves you will know your error in piling up wealth and children.

**كلا** (kallā): That is, indeed.

**لو تعلمون علم اليقين** (law ta'lamūna 'ilma al-yaqīn): That is, if you had certain knowledge of the outcome of piling up wealth, you would not have boasted of the abundance of your riches.

**لترون الجحيم** (latarawunna al-jaḥīm): That is, the Fire.

**يومئذ** (yawma'idhin): That is, on the day you see Hellfire with the eye of certainty.

**عن النعيم** (ʿani al-naʿīm): That is, the blessings you enjoyed and delighted in: health, leisure, security, food and drink.

**Meaning of the verses:**

God, the Exalted, says ﴿Your preoccupation with piling up [wealth] has diverted you﴾. This is God's address to those who busy themselves with gathering wealth and multiplying it for the sake of showing off and boasting, a preoccupation that diverted them from obeying God and His Messenger, so that they died without sending forward any good for themselves. So God says to them: "alhākum", that is, the piling up occupied you, namely in wealth, for the sake of boasting and showing off its abundance. ﴿Until you visited the graves﴾: that is, after your death you were carried to them to remain in them until you are brought out from them for reckoning and recompense, that is, on the Day of Resurrection.

His words to them, ﴿Nay﴾, mean: this is not how you ought to act, so refrain from this conduct which leads you to ruin and loss. ﴿You will come to know﴾: the outcome of your preoccupation with disobeying God and His Messenger and with neglecting provision for the Hereafter. ﴿Again, nay, you will come to know﴾: He repeated the warning and the threat.

His words ﴿Nay, if you knew with certainty﴾ mean: indeed, if you knew what you will find in your graves and on the Day of your raising and resurrection, you would not have occupied yourselves with wealth and competed in it. His words ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire, and again you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ are the answer to an oath, like "By Our might, you will surely see Hellfire," that is, the Fire, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. The polytheist sees it and burns in it, while the believer sees it and God saves him from it. ﴿Again, you will see it with the eye of certainty﴾: that is, the matter about which there is no doubt, when Hell will be brought forth and all the people of the gathering will see it.

His words ﴿Then on that day you will surely be questioned﴾, that is, on the day you see Hellfire with the eye of certainty, ﴿about the blessings﴾ that you had in the world: health, leisure, security, food and drink. Whoever gives thanks for them will be saved, and whoever does not give thanks for them will be held to account. He will not be excused except for a garment that covers the nakedness, a morsel of bread that stills hunger, and a shelter that protects from heat and cold.

It is authentically related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and Amr ibn al-Tayyihan: «This is among the blessings about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection,» pointing to dates, fresh dates, and cold water. It is also authentically related: «The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about his life, how he spent it; about his youth, how he wore it out; about his knowledge, what he did with it; and about his wealth, where he acquired it and how he spent it.»

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. A warning against gathering and multiplying wealth while not giving thanks for it and abandoning obedience to God and His Messenger for its sake.

2. Affirmation of the punishment of the grave, confirmed by His words "until you visit the graves; nay, you will come to know," that is, in the grave.

3. Establishing the doctrine of resurrection and the inevitability of recompense after reckoning, interrogation and questioning.

4. The inevitability of a servant being questioned about the blessings God bestowed upon him in the world. If he was grateful for them, he succeeds; if he was ungrateful for them, he is seized, God forbid.

**حتى زرتم المقابر** (ḥattā zurtumu al-maqābir): That is, you were preoccupied with gathering wealth and boasting of its abundance until you died and were carried to the graveyards.

**كلا** (kallā): That is, this is not how you should behave, so refrain from this piling up.

**سوف تعلمون** (sawfa ta'lamūn): That is, when you enter your graves you will know your error in piling up wealth and children.

**كلا** (kallā): That is, indeed.

**لو تعلمون علم اليقين** (law ta'lamūna 'ilma al-yaqīn): That is, if you had certain knowledge of the outcome of piling up wealth, you would not have boasted of the abundance of your riches.

**لترون الجحيم** (latarawunna al-jaḥīm): That is, the Fire.

**يومئذ** (yawma'idhin): That is, on the day you see Hellfire with the eye of certainty.

**عن النعيم** (ʿani al-naʿīm): That is, the blessings you enjoyed and delighted in: health, leisure, security, food and drink.

**Meaning of the verses:**

God, the Exalted, says ﴿Your preoccupation with piling up [wealth] has diverted you﴾. This is God's address to those who busy themselves with gathering wealth and multiplying it for the sake of showing off and boasting, a preoccupation that diverted them from obeying God and His Messenger, so that they died without sending forward any good for themselves. So God says to them: "alhākum", that is, the piling up occupied you, namely in wealth, for the sake of boasting and showing off its abundance. ﴿Until you visited the graves﴾: that is, after your death you were carried to them to remain in them until you are brought out from them for reckoning and recompense, that is, on the Day of Resurrection.

His words to them, ﴿Nay﴾, mean: this is not how you ought to act, so refrain from this conduct which leads you to ruin and loss. ﴿You will come to know﴾: the outcome of your preoccupation with disobeying God and His Messenger and with neglecting provision for the Hereafter. ﴿Again, nay, you will come to know﴾: He repeated the warning and the threat.

His words ﴿Nay, if you knew with certainty﴾ mean: indeed, if you knew what you will find in your graves and on the Day of your raising and resurrection, you would not have occupied yourselves with wealth and competed in it. His words ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire, and again you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ are the answer to an oath, like "By Our might, you will surely see Hellfire," that is, the Fire, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. The polytheist sees it and burns in it, while the believer sees it and God saves him from it. ﴿Again, you will see it with the eye of certainty﴾: that is, the matter about which there is no doubt, when Hell will be brought forth and all the people of the gathering will see it.

His words ﴿Then on that day you will surely be questioned﴾, that is, on the day you see Hellfire with the eye of certainty, ﴿about the blessings﴾ that you had in the world: health, leisure, security, food and drink. Whoever gives thanks for them will be saved, and whoever does not give thanks for them will be held to account. He will not be excused except for a garment that covers the nakedness, a morsel of bread that stills hunger, and a shelter that protects from heat and cold.

It is authentically related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr and Amr ibn al-Tayyihan: «This is among the blessings about which you will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection,» pointing to dates, fresh dates, and cold water. It is also authentically related: «The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about his life, how he spent it; about his youth, how he wore it out; about his knowledge, what he did with it; and about his wealth, where he acquired it and how he spent it.»

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. A warning against gathering and multiplying wealth while not giving thanks for it and abandoning obedience to God and His Messenger for its sake.

2. Affirmation of the punishment of the grave, confirmed by His words "until you visit the graves; nay, you will come to know," that is, in the grave.

3. Establishing the doctrine of resurrection and the inevitability of recompense after reckoning, interrogation and questioning.

4. The inevitability of a servant being questioned about the blessings God bestowed upon him in the world. If he was grateful for them, he succeeds; if he was ungrateful for them, he is seized, God forbid.
